newsitem.title: USA: Nantucket sees Q4, FY 1996 net loss.
newsitem.headline: Nantucket sees Q4, FY 1996 net loss.

text.p: Nantucket Industries Inc said Tuesday it expects to post a loss in the fourth quarter as well as for the fiscal year because of production and quality problems.
The company said it had canceled customer orders for new products in the third quarter ended November 30 because of production delays and quality issues involving foreign manufacturing contractors.
An expected increase in shipments in the fourth quarter will not materialize because of ongoing production and quality issues with its foreign manufacturing contractors, it said.
Chairman and Chief Executive Stephen Samberg said in a statement that Nantucket is implementing a number of operational changes to prevent a recurrence of the issues it faced this fiscal year.
Those steps include on-site management and supervision, as well as finding new foreign manufacturing contractors, it said. The company said it also has begun cutting costs to lower its overhead.

For the third quarter, the company reported a net loss of $862,000, or $0.27 per share, on sales of $8.44 million. In the prior year's third quarter, the company reported a net profit of $498,000, or $0.17 per share, on sales of $9.85 million.
